coverageSemantics.exact: Retains the authored value expression and the listed runtime scenario. This is not a claim that every original source-string assertion, fixture read count, or CLR exception type is checked by HTTP execution. Equivalent original expressions share factories; distinct expressions in a multi-action factory remain separate SDK calls and observable result fields.
coverageSemantics.representative: Expression, destination, seed, or observed assertion differs, or only part of the original multi-observation contract is covered; the reason records the limitation.
coverageSemantics.authoring-contract: Checks actual SDK construction/GetActionDefinition without executing emitted code or contacting managed connectors. Only after the check passes does a codeless proof workflow return authoring-contract passed. That response is NOT runtime execution evidence for the inspected or rejected expression.
coverageSemantics.compile-diagnostic: Standalone negative source in CompileCases/*.cs.txt, intentionally excluded from default Compile. Compile separately against each SDK; do not count these as successful workflows.
coverageSemantics.runtime-property-contract: Executes the original nondeterministic expression and validates its documented runtime properties independently for each SDK. BothSatisfyNondeterministicContract means both satisfy the property contract, NOT that their returned values are equal.
coverageSemantics.blocked: No runnable/authoring reproduction; reason must identify the concrete blocker and original evidence.

limitations: No emitted expression or generated JSON is edited. There is no local fake expression evaluator.
Factories are shared verbatim by both SDK builds. Only the parent runner builds and starts actual hosts.

SDK seed constructors remain inline in each case. Response value lambdas also stay at their case call sites; shared Finish only connects an already-authored graph. F010/F028 intentionally retain source-visible helper authoring because that is the original behavior under test.
Source-only mismatches can execute equivalently. F177 is a known both-SDK runtime success, not a runtime defect.
F005 original scalar-null Compose is invalid on both real hosts. Its object-valued correction preserves null in a valid payload; F070 and F039 use the same explicit destination distinction.

Expected failed workflows retain a normal Response referencing Result, but Response is skipped when Result fails. They require ExpectedRunStatus=Failed, ExpectedHttpStatus=502 and a matching ExpectedActionError substring. A generic failed run, compilation rejection, or NoResponse body alone cannot satisfy the intended error contract.

Multi-action workflows expose every result field on success. A first failing action can skip later actions on the same SDK; consult action statuses rather than treating skipped assertions as verified failures.
Connector schema, encoding, managed trigger and callback checks are authoring-contracts, not live Service Bus/Azure Queue/Agent requests.
Expression-tree precomputation F086 is represented by an already computed scalar, avoiding invocation of a runtime value lambda during workflow generation.
Original mock-host getter read counters are not available on the actual host. Short-circuit and single-read mappings state this limitation.

Ordinary paired workflow inputs and seeds are deterministic. F139 intentionally returns the original DateTime.UtcNow value unchanged under ResponseContract=UtcTimestamp: each run must return UTC within its own invocation/end window. Paired timestamps are never compared for value equality; the result category is BothSatisfyNondeterministicContract. No random Guid or runtime counter values are returned.
Compilation and actual host results are produced by the parent runner and are not asserted by this coverage document.

customCodeSeedSafety.sdkBehavior: CustomCode<T> emits CSharpScriptCode with inputs.userFunctionName only. There is no inline script, connector, URI, connection or external input in these actions. The SDK registers the compiled delegate through ScriptExecutor.SaveCustomCodeMethodInfo during definition generation; inspection here never invokes the callback.
customCodeSeedSafety.review: All nine seed actions across seven workflows ignore WorkflowContext and return Task.FromResult of fixed in-memory data. They perform no network, filesystem, storage, Agent/LLM, process, clock, random or environment access. Items(bool) only creates an ItemsList, arrays, dictionaries and JValue literals. The invalid case deliberately changes active to the string invalid for a downstream conversion failure.
customCodeSeedSafety.allowlisting: The parent owns runtime safety policy. These are reviewed candidates, not authorization to allow arbitrary CSharpScriptCode. The original anonymous callbacks failed with Non-static method requires a target because ScriptExecutor.InvokeParameters invokes MethodInfo with null. Seed-only adaptation now uses the exact named static callbacks below, so parent safety matching must use those names instead of the old <Case>b__ prefix. SDK action construction and tested expressions remain inline and unchanged.
customCodeSeedSafety.inputEvidence: Expected current inputs follow directly from CSharpScriptCode.GetActionDefinition assigning callback.Method.Name. Source was not rebuilt after this adaptation while Andrew assets were active; parent must rebuild/export and verify actual inputs before staging.
